HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

options.label: Creative computing, design & digital society
options.concept: Combine programming, machine learning and data analysis with product prototyping, creative communication and user research. Study how people and organisations use digital products and how choices about fairness and accountability shape their development.

options.label: AI, data & smart systems
options.concept: Use programming, algorithms and machine learning to analyse data and model smart systems. Study signals and probability, and apply mathematics to robot motion and planning. Ethics and market research add perspectives on how such systems are used.

options.label: Human-centred interaction & technology
options.concept: Study how perception, language and social behaviour influence people’s interactions with technology. Combine psychology, qualitative research and product prototyping with data analysis, creative communication and responsible digital innovation.

analysis: The broad option connects computing with prototyping and qualitative and experimental user research. AI Ethics explicitly covers fairness, privacy and accountability and provides a real partial link with Humane by Design. It does not reproduce the future-design studio or the dedicated fairness unit. Creative Communication Laboratory adds creative practice through language, sound, performance and hybrid media, distinct from an electronics or installation studio. The smart systems option distinguishes itself through robotics, signal analysis, numerical methods, linear algebra and probability. Robotics contributes computational motion, kinematics and manipulation. The human option distinguishes itself through biopsychology, social psychology, language, perception, attention and organisational behaviour. It gains qualitative research methodology and creative experimentation while retaining product prototyping and market research. Psycholinguistics runs in term two after Brain and Behaviour. The first pair differs by 37.5 EC each way and the other pairs by 52.5 and 90 EC, with different taught methods and problems. The selected product design course includes interviews, fabrication planning, prototyping and testing. Its contribution is substantial even though it is broader than HCI. Database Management Systems, Perception & Action, Psycholinguistics, Strategy & Digital Transformation and Market Research contribute within their documented scope. None of the plans supplies the complete physical computing and electronics workshop sequence.

alignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming addresses the programming foundation inside this broad introductory module, without reproducing its full multidisciplinary scope.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data processing and visualisation, while the comparator module additionally physicalises data through an installation.
Machine Learning directly addresses the AI and machine-learning core, without the comparator's dedicated-hardware project.
Twente integrates programming, physical computing, circuits and visualisation in a smart-environment project.
Both frame problems around users and consider how ideas can become solutions. UCR focuses on entrepreneurship and value propositions.
Consumer Product Design directly develops user-needs analysis, prototyping and iterative evaluation, while the comparator focuses specifically on human-computer interaction.
Both examine the social effects of technical choices. UCR’s AI Ethics covers fairness, bias and accountability, while Humane by Design also develops future scenarios and design projects.
Both develop written argument and communication. The Amsterdam course applies academic writing to the graduation project.
Both explore how creative choices shape an audience’s experience. UCR works through language, sound and performance, while Twente develops interactive installations.
Twente reserves 30 EC for approved electives, a minor or exchange.
Twente requires an individual design and research project. UCR offers independent research separately.
The graduation semester includes a dedicated reflection unit tied to the design project.
